sentences.text:
This criminal revision has been filed against the judgment and order dated 22.05.2003 passed by learned Special Judge (S.C./S.T. Act), Varanasi dismissing the Appeal No. 193 of 1993, Raj Kumar and another Vs. State of U.P. and another, arising out of judgement and order dated 15.10.1999 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Varanasi in Criminal Case No. 6036 of 1994,
State Vs. Raj Kumar and another, convicting the revisionists under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentencing them to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months and to pay a fine of Rs. 1000/- each.

sentences.text: It has been averred in the instant revision that the trail Court has erred in believing the testimony of the witnesses.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: He has further argued that whole approach of the trial Court, convicting and sentencing the accused-revisionist is incorrect.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: The impugned judgment and order suffers from gross illegality, which has resulted in miscarriage of justice and, therefore, this Court, in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 397/401 CrPC, should set-aside the impugned judgment and order passed by the Courts below be set aside and the accused-revisionist is liable to be acquitted from the charges levelled against him.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned A.G.A. has submitted that the trial Court has correctly analyzed the evidence,
and has come to correct conclusion that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused-revisionist.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: He has further submitted that the impugned judgment and order has been passed by the trial Court after analyzing the evidence in detail, which is not liable to be interfered with by this Court in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 397/401 CrPC.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text:
He has further submitted that the view taken by the Courts below is not an impossible view and, therefore,
this Court should not interfere with the order of conviction, and he has prayed for dismissal of the revision.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: I have considered the pleadings made in the present revision, submissions advanced by the learned Additional Government Advocate, representing respondent-State, including the evidence led by the prosecution in support of its case.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: The revision jurisdiction of the High Court as contemplated under Section 401 of Cr.P.C. operates within narrow limits and can be exercised only in exceptional cases where interests of public justice require interference for the correction of gross miscarriage of justice.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: It cannot be exercised because the lower court has taken a wrong view of the law or mis-appreciated evidence on record.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: The revision power of the High Court is to be exercised when there is manifest error of law or glaring defect in the procedure.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: In the instant case close scrutiny of evidence reveals that on the basis of evidence, learned trial Court has rendered that the prosecution version was established.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: Considering entire evidence, it cannot be said that findings rendered by learned trial Court are perverse or suffers from any illegality or error of jurisdiction.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: It is well settled that the revision Court generally would not re-appreciate evidence and would not substitute findings of fact unless the findings of Court below is not based on evidence or suffers from perversity or illegality.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: It is also well settled that if on the basis of evidence two views are possible, the view favourable to accused persons has to be taken.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: In the instant case, considering entire evidence it cannot be said that impugned judgment and orders suffer from any such illegality, perversity or error of jurisdiction so as to warrant any interference by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: In view of above, the instant revision lacks merit and is, accordingly dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 11 November, 2022.json

sentences.text: In case, the accused-revisionist has not deposited the amount of fine, he is directed to deposit the amount of fine before the concerned Court below, as directed by the trial Court within a period of 45 days from today.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that the complainant, Food Inspector inspected the shop of revisionists where flour, pulses, spices, sugar, jaggery and biscuits were placed for sale.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: The complainant served notice in Form No. 6 and purchased 7.50 gms. Pulse for Rs. 8.25/kg. and divided it in three equal parts and sampled it as per provisions of law.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Accused was sought to sign it for which he denied.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: The worker in the shop of accused Girdhar signed the complain as a witness.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, they prepared sample and sent it to laboratory for analysis to CMO concerned on 16.12.1991.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: As per analysis report No. 16917, 1% Dal Keshari was found adulterated with the sample which is prohibited as edible goods.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: After the analysis report, complainant filed the complaint forwarded through the Medical Officer under Section 2(1)(l) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 which is punishable under Section 7/16 of the Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: After the written consent of Medical Officer, the complaint is filed.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 5. Accused were summoned in the Court, the statement of witness, Gaya Prasad Singh was recorded under Section 244 of Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: The Court framed charges against accused under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and read over to the accused and the accused denied from the charges and seek trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. The complainant Gaya Prasad Singh was again produced to record his evidence under Section 246 of Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The prosecution produced PW-2 Ram Janam Yadav, Food Clerk in Municipal Board,
PW-3 Ashok Kumar Srivastava, Food Clerk in the office of Varanasi.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text:
After the conclusion of prosecution witnesses, statements of accused were recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
7.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Accused stated on oath in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. that whole incident is wrong, no such incident happened, Food Inspector did not inspected his shop, no sample was collected by him, no papers were signed by him at the time of inspection he was not present at shop.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Accused Dashrath also stated in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. that he was not present at shop at the relevant point of time when the sample was collected by the Food Inspector.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8. Accused were awarded the opportunity of producing defence evidence but the accused did not produce any defence witness.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Hence learned trial court found on the basis of the evidence on prosecution and on the basis of Laboratory Analysis Report that the sample collected by Food Inspector was adulterated.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Learned trial court relying upon Ram Lubhaya Vs. Municipal Corporation Delhi, 1974 (4) SCC 491, State of U.P. Vs. Badri EFR 1998 (2), 2192-2020 and Halku Vs. State of U.P. EFR 1986, 100 and 101 held that, according to sections 10(7) of the Food Adulteration Act, it is mandatory to inspect the shop in the presence of independent witnesses but it is held by the Supreme Court that he need not be produced before this court for their evidence hence compliance of section 10(7) of the Food Adulteration Act has been followed properly in accordance with law.
10. On the basis of food analysis report which was proved by the witnesses, the court held that sample contains moisture of 5.8% and adulteration of Dal Khesari of 0.7%, however, the sample was not found broken or damaged by insects.

sentences.text: No chemical adulteration was found with the sample hence learned trial court found that only 1% Dal Khesari was found adulterated which is prohibited as edible goods hence convicted the accused under Section 7/16 and punished them for simple imprisonment of 6 months and fine of Rs.1000/- each.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 11. Aggrieved with the judgment passed by Special Chief Judicial Magistrate-I, Varanasi, the revisionists preferred criminal revision.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text:
12. The first revisional court, going through the record and judgment passed by the Special Chief Judicial Magistrate-I, held that the finding recorded by learned trial court is well reasoned and does not suffer any illegality or material irregularity and needs no interference and, confirmed the judgment passed by Special Judge (S.C & S.T.) Act dated 22.5.2003.
13.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for revisionists submits that as per analysis report, no chemical adulteration is found, the sample is not found damaged, the moisture of 5.8% was found, rest of the sample that is 99.3% was found up to the mark.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learning trial code as well as revisional code did not consider the fact that the sample was 99.3%.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: As per prescribed standard the revisionists are not previously convict nor wanted in any other case except the instant one.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The complainant Food Inspector did not obtain the signature of accused revisionists on samples or complaint, there is no independent witness to the incident hence it is prayed to set aside the judgment and order dated 15.10.1999 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-I as well as judgment and order passed by revisional court dated 22.5.2003.
14.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. submits that notice was duly served on accused, however, they refused to sign it.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: The signature of their servant is taken on the complaint.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is also stated in the complaint itself that no independent witness agreed to sign the papers.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: The sample was prepared according to the provisions of law and sent for analysis.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: As per analysis report proved by complainant 0.7% Khesari found adulterated in Dal Chana.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that as per the provisions of section 10(7), it is a mandatory requirement of law that sample should be prepared in front of one of the independent witness but it is not the requirement of law to produce them in court also.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The Peon of revisionists,
Girdhar Ram has signed the document, complainant and samples, however he could not be produced as evidence.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: He is the servant of revisionists hence the judgement passed by the trial court suffers no irregularity and the revision is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: 16. The main contention of learned counsel for the revisionists is that the learned trial court as well as first revisional court analyzed the evidence of witnesses in arbitrary manner and no public witness has been produced by prosecution, the mandatory provisions are not complied with.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Section 10(7) of the Food Adulteration Act states as under:-
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Where the food inspector take any action under clause (a) of Sub-section 1 and Sub-section 2, Sub-section 4, Sub-section 6, he shall call one or more persons to be present at the time when such action is taken and take his or their signature.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 17. Learned counsel for the revisionists submits that the independent witness has not been produced in court during trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: The provisions of Section 10(7) envisages the signature of independent witness or complaint on samples, however, it does not contemplate the evidence of that person during the trial too.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 18. Hon'ble Apex Court held in Ram Lubhaya Vs. Municipal Corporation Delhi 1974 (4) SCC 491 that, it is mandatory to summon independent witness at the place of occurrence at the relevant time but there examination during trial is not necessary.

entities.text: Ram Lubhaya Vs. Municipal Corporation Delhi 1974 (4) SCC 491
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Section 10(7) stipulates that food inspector shall call one or more person for witnessing the proceedings of inspection, however, if they refuse for signature or cooperate with the proceedings, the Food Inspector cannot compel them for evidence.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 19. In the given case, the complainant tried to summon many persons for signature on the papers as witness but they refused to participate in the proceedings, however, Peon of revisionists himself signed the papers, therefore, it cannot be termed as illegal proceedings because prosecution has undertaken the provisions of Food Adulteration Rules.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 20. The second contention of learned counsel for the revisionists is that sample do not contain any material, injurious to the health of any person.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: No chemical adulteration is found.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: No broken or damaged or insecticide grain is found according to food analysis report and learned trial court did not take into consideration the above mentioned facts.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 21. I have gone through the analysis report, wherein it is specifically mentioned that 0.7% Dal Khesari is found adulterated in Chana Dal, which is injurious to the health hence prosecution proved the factum of adulteration by cogent piece of evidence and supported it by the oral evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: Revisionists are also given opportunity to adduce defence, however, no defence is produced except the bare statement of denial.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: 22. Accused/revisionists did not disclose any prior enmity between the revisionists and the complainant, Food Inspector.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: No ulterior motive to falsify the complaint is mentioned by the accused revisionists.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text: PW-1, Food Inspector has acted in compliance of his statutory duties imposed upon him.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

There is nothing on record to suggest that the evidence of complainant is false or fabricated,
therefore, the evidence of Food Inspector cannot be brushed aside merely because he is complainant to the case and there is no independent witness.

sentences.text: 24. During the course of argument learned counsel for the revisionists submitted that in case the court upheld the conviction of revisionists, the punishment may be reduced.
sentences._hearing_file: Raj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 March, 2024.json

sentences.text:
It is submitted that this case is 23 years old, both the revisionists are old age, they are not previously convict nor they have committed any crime after this incident, the court has not given them the benefit of First Offenders Act, he had been detained in jail for 7 days he is ready to deposit the fine whichever is decided by this Court, hence it is prayed to commute the sentence.

He has further submitted that the view taken by the Courts below is not an impossible view and, therefore,
this Court should not interfere with the order of conviction, and he has prayed for dismissal of the revision.
opennyai_summary.11_November_2022__ANALYSIS:
The revision jurisdiction of the High Court as contemplated under Section 401 of Cr.P.C. operates within narrow limits and can be exercised only in exceptional cases where interests of public justice require interference for the correction of gross miscarriage of justice.
It cannot be exercised because the lower court has taken a wrong view of the law or mis-appreciated evidence on record.
The revision power of the High Court is to be exercised when there is manifest error of law or glaring defect in the procedure.
In the instant case close scrutiny of evidence reveals that on the basis of evidence, learned trial Court has rendered that the prosecution version was established.
Considering entire evidence, it cannot be said that findings rendered by learned trial Court are perverse or suffers from any illegality or error of jurisdiction.
It is well settled that the revision Court generally would not re-appreciate evidence and would not substitute findings of fact unless the findings of Court below is not based on evidence or suffers from perversity or illegality.
In the instant case, considering entire evidence it cannot be said that impugned judgment and orders suffer from any such illegality, perversity or error of jurisdiction so as to warrant any interference by this Court.
opennyai_summary.11_November_2022__decision:
In view of above, the instant revision lacks merit and is, accordingly dismissed.
In case, the accused-revisionist has not deposited the amount of fine, he is directed to deposit the amount of fine before the concerned Court below, as directed by the trial Court within a period of 45 days from today.
